name: @kanzo-tech/graph
description: Kanzo graph view — a GraphAr graph attached to the page's DuckDB, read through the page's Mosaic coordinator as one more client, laid out and drawn with cosmos.gl on the GPU. Sibling of @kanzo-tech/ui, not part of it: the admission rules exclude graphs from the generic vocabulary by name.
//peers: All required. cosmos.gl draws and lays out; `@ark-ui/react` is what every part renders through (`ark.*`), a peer for the reason it is `@kanzo-tech/ui`'s — two copies of Ark would be two portals and two focus traps; `lucide-react` is the icon set the parts draw their buttons with, `@kanzo-tech/ui`'s own peer; `@kanzo-tech/mosaic` is the coordinator the graph reads through as a client, and the crossfilter it listens to and publishes into. The Mosaic stack itself — mosaic-core, mosaic-sql — is `@kanzo-tech/mosaic`'s peer, declared once there. `tailwind-variants` is a dependency, as it is `ui`'s and `ai`'s: the parts write their appearance as recipes, which is also what puts this package under the guards (`packages/ui/src/guard-corpus.ts`).
//graphar: The graph reads an Apache GraphAr graph through the `Graph` `@kanzo-tech/graphar-duckdb`'s `attachGraph` answers, and through nothing else: its types and their counts and properties, `links` for the edges, `vertex` for the inspector, `search` for the search, and each type's `table` and `index` as the `Graph` names them. It writes no name of the format. The global id, `dense_id`, is this package's arithmetic over the per-type index, each type's `first` its offset in the graph's order (`src/core/source.ts`).
//gauges: One gauge per published entry, and one per tree-shaken import a consumer meets; `scripts/gauges.mjs` (through `.size-limit.mjs`) is what each measures, and every limit's reason — each raise, dated, with its before and after — is a row on /docs/design, *A gauge per entry, and its raises written here*.
